headline: WSJ reports Iran is giving Ansar Allah targeting and intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia
dek: WSJ, citing people briefed on Saudi and Yemeni anti-Ansar Allah alliance intelligence: Iran's support has enabled the Ansar Allah' 'most potent and sophisticated attacks yet' on Saudi Arabia and Yemeni allies — help selecting drone/missile targets, training, intelligence and tactical guidance —…
sources: Wall Street Journal — 'Iran Is Giving Ansar Allah Targeting and Intelligence for Attacks on Saudi Arabia' (wsj.com/world/middle-east/iran-houthi-saudi-arabia-attacks-38b82107); corroborated by JPost (2026-10-17 08:46), Times
fault_line: Is Iran running the Ansar Allah war (WSJ/intel briefings) or are the Ansar Allah fighting their own war (Tehran's denial + mediation offer)?

sections.what_happened: WSJ, citing people briefed on Saudi and Yemeni anti-Ansar Allah alliance intelligence: Iran's support has enabled the Ansar Allah' 'most potent and sophisticated attacks yet' on Saudi Arabia and Yemeni allies — help selecting drone/missile targets, training, intelligence and tactical guidance — contributing to rapid Ansar Allah territorial gains and control of Yemen's Bab al-Mandeb coastline. Named voices: Danny Citrinowicz (former head of Iran branch, Israeli defense intelligence): 'The connection is very, very strong on the operational level... a shared strategic interest that isn't based on a client-patron relationship, but rather on strategic cooperation.' Adam Baron (New America): Iranian assistance 'undeniably paved the way for the rapid-fire gains.' Soufan Center: strikes 'helping Iran project power.'
sections.what_verified: JPost, TOI, Times of Israel, lb.ua, Tribune India, MK (Yonhap) all carry the WSJ reporting; facts on recent strikes (Riyadh airport ~13-17 killed, King Khalid airport strikes, Bab al-Mandeb coastline control) consistent with prior scan records
sections.what_disputed: STRONG: Iran FM spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei (Oct 16, 2026; via CNA/Punch/Diplomatic Insight): 'The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Ansar Allah) operations'; reiterated mediation offer. Ansar Allah themselves dismiss Iranian-support claims as baseless (per MK report). Named expert voices include a former Israeli intelligence official — assess source framing. The WSJ's core sourcing = unnamed briefings from Saudi and anti-Ansar Allah alliance intelligence — parties with motive to magnify Iran's role.
sections.why_matters: Iran says it is NOT in the Ansar Allah fight — and offers to mediate. WSJ's answer to its own unnamed intel: a former Israeli intel chief and a Washington think-tanker. Show both, name every source; the evidence question IS the story. Anchor card: the two quotes side by side (Baqaei vs Citrinowicz).
sections.context: Background: Iran/Yemen/Saudi — NEW: WSJ reports Iran is giving Ansar Allah targeting and intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia

totw_analysis: Our read: Iran says it is NOT in the Ansar Allah fight — and offers to mediate. WSJ's answer to its own unnamed intel: a former Israeli intel chief and a Washington think-tanker. Show both, name every source; the evidence question IS the story. Anchor card: the two quotes side by side (Baqaei vs Citrinowicz).
